title: The Ticklish Lion
summary: Leo has just become king of the savannah, and every morning he has to roar from the big rock. The trouble is, the wind tickles his mane.

scenes.text:
On the savannah, every morning, the king wakes all the animals with a roar.

For many years, the king had been Grandpa Lion. But Grandpa was old now and wanted to sleep in. So that day, for the very first time, it was Leo's turn.

Leo climbed up onto the big rock. Down below, the giraffes, the elephants and the zebras waited in silence.

Leo took a deep breath. He puffed out his chest. He opened his enormous mouth…

And at that very moment, along came the wind.

It slipped into his mane, it tickled his ears, and…

"Hee, hee, hee!" Out it came. "Ha, ha, ha!"

The animals looked at one another. Leo covered his muzzle with both paws, red as a tomato, and ran off to hide.

Behind a bush, Suri the meerkat found him. She was his best friend.

"What happened up there?"

"It's the tickles," whispered Leo. "When the air ruffles my mane, it tickles. It always has. But I've never told anyone."

Suri scratched her head.

"Then we'll have to fix it before tomorrow."

First, she tied his mane up with a vine, nice and tight, so the air couldn't move it.

Leo looked at himself in a puddle. He looked like a broom.

And that made him laugh so hard that the vine came undone.

"Second idea," said Suri. "You'll roar inside a cave, where the air can't get in."

Leo went into the cave and roared. And out came a magnificent roar, enormous, a real king's roar.

But from inside the cave, nobody heard it. Only a bat hanging from the ceiling, who woke up in a very bad mood.

"Third idea," said Suri. "Mud."

She grabbed a handful of mud and threw it at his mane. Splat!

His mane went stiff as a stone. The air couldn't move it any more. But when the mud started to dry, it itched. It itched terribly.

And Leo scratched, and scratched, and rolled about on the ground, laughing his head off.

The next morning, Leo climbed onto the big rock again, with his mane freshly washed and his heart very small.

Down below, the whole savannah was waiting.

Leo took a deep breath. He puffed out his chest. He opened his mouth…

And along came a gust.

Leo clenched his teeth. He held on. He held on. He held on…

And he let out the biggest burst of laughter ever heard on the savannah.

There was a silence.

Then a giraffe gave a little giggle. Then an elephant. Then the zebras, the monkeys, the wildebeest and even the hippos, with their mouths open like drawers.

The whole savannah woke up laughing.

Grandpa Lion peeked out from his shady spot, his mane all messy and his face still sleepy.

"What's all this racket?" he asked.

"I'm sorry, Grandpa," said Leo. "I tried to roar. But my mane gets tickly."

Grandpa was quiet for a moment. Then he came closer and whispered in his ear:

"Mine too. That's why I always roared so fast."

And the two of them laughed together, the old king and the new one.

Ever since that day, nobody on the savannah wakes up to a roar. They wake up to a laugh. And the animals say the day starts much, much better that way.
